note: Twig Real Content is a single Twig extension exposing a test and a filter both named real_content. No config, routes, permissions, schema, Drush, or plugins. The callables: return empty/FALSE for an empty render array, require an already-rendered string/MarkupInterface (else throw TwigRealContentException), then strip_tags() keeping an allowlist (img, iframe, video, svg, object, embed, input, hr, script, style, link, source, drupal-render-placeholder) and trim; the test returns TRUE if anything remains, the filter returns the stripped string. Because there is no config, medium cases store a known markup string in Drupal state for the agent to fetch and evaluate; hard cases have the agent apply the real_content filter/test to a state-provided input and store the result, verified by recomputing with the live extension (new TwigRealContentTwigExtension()). All state keys are namespaced twig_real_content_*.

evals.prompt: In a Drupal Twig template, core's `{% if page.sidebar %}` is true even when the sidebar renders only empty wrapper markup. Which Twig test/filter does the twig_real_content module add to check whether a region actually has meaningful content?
evals.expected_output: It adds a Twig test and filter both named real_content, e.g. `{% if page.sidebar|render is real_content %}` or `{{ var|real_content }}`.

evals.prompt: Using twig_real_content, why does `{% if page.sidebar is real_content %}` throw a TwigRealContentException, and what must you do to the variable first?
evals.expected_output: The test/filter expects an already-rendered string (or MarkupInterface); a raw render array throws TwigRealContentException. Render or capture it first: `{% if page.sidebar|render is real_content %}`.

evals.prompt: With twig_real_content, does a region that contains only an (and no text) count as real content? Name some of the HTML tags it treats as meaningful even without text.
evals.expected_output: Yes. strip_tags() keeps an allowlist of self-meaningful tags — img, iframe, video, svg, object, embed, input, hr, script, style, link, source, drupal-render-placeholder — so an image-only region is real content (test returns TRUE).

evals.prompt: This Drupal site has a value in the state system under the key twig_real_content_probe holding a rendered markup string. Fetch it and, using the twig_real_content module's rules, determine whether that markup would count as real content (i.e. would its region be non-empty). Explain the result.
evals.expected_output:
The stored markup is `
\n\t
` — only an empty wrapper and whitespace. After strip_tags()+trim nothing remains, so the real_content filter returns '' and the test returns FALSE: it is NOT real content (the region is empty).
